reason: Claim c1 is confirmed, in_scope, and backed by scope evidence from the operative contract (problem.txt, the artifact's only contract source since no test.py/get_inputs exist): the target is out[b,k] = sum_j x[b,j]*omega_N^(j*k) mod 3329 in natural order with exact equality (abs/rel tol 0). Runtime probe t9 (exit 0) shows kernel.run output mismatches reference on canonical field-valued inputs for both N=64 and N=128, including simple impulse rows — e.g. N=64 impulse at position 32 gives kernel 2293 vs reference 1 at output column 0. The reference is a finite, well-defined modular DFT, so this is a genuine correctness failure, not a reference-undefined or tie-breaking artifact. The contract's "any modular-reduction algorithm" clause permits alternative internal methods but requires the same exact result, so the deviation is a defect regardless of root cause (twiddle convention or otherwise). c3 (bank layout mismatch) was rebutted by probe t11. c2 remains inconclusive because its probe tested _multiply against plain product % 3329 instead of the correct Montgomery/REDC semantics; I set it aside as redundant since c1 alone establishes a decisive exact-equality failure. Verdict: reject.
